item.title: Southern University System Presidential Search Committee announces finalists for system president
item.description:
The Southern University System Presidential Search Committee today announced the selection of three finalists for the position of president of the Southern University System, marking a significant milestone in the search for the next leader of the nation's only historically Black university system.
Following a comprehensive review and evaluation of candidates, including in-person interviews with six semifinalists, the committee selected the following individuals to advance to the final stage of the search process:
 
Brian K. Bridges, Ph.D.
Senior Advisor, Whiteboard Advisors
Former Secretary of Higher Education, State of New Jersey (2020-2025)
Roscoe Jones, J.D.
Former Dean, Drake University Law School 
Larissa Littleton-Steib, Ph.D.
Chancellor, Delgado Community College
 
The finalists were selected following a thorough evaluation of their professional qualifications, leadership experience, demonstrated accomplishments, and vision for advancing the Southern University System's mission of academic excellence, research, innovation, and public service.
 
“This has been a thoughtful, rigorous and deliberate process, and I commend the members of the Southern University System Presidential Search Committee for their dedication and commitment to identifying exceptional leaders who understand the unique mission and opportunities of the Southern University System,” said Jason Hughes, chair of the Presidential Search Committee. “Our committee approached this responsibility with a shared commitment to transparency and fairness to identify candidates with the experience, vision, and leadership necessary to guide the System into its next chapter. We are confident that the finalists we are advancing to the Board of Supervisors represent strong candidates who are well-positioned to build upon Southern's legacy while advancing its future.”
The national search has been conducted with the assistance of TM² Executive Search, which has supported the committee throughout the recruitment, candidate evaluation and selection process. The search has also included opportunities for engagement with faculty, staff, students, alumni and other stakeholders across the Southern University System.
 
Next Steps in the Presidential Search
The finalists will now advance to the Southern University System Board of Supervisors for interviews and further consideration. The Board will conduct interviews with the finalists before making its final selection of the next System president.
Additional information regarding the schedule and format of the Board interviews will be announced as details are finalized.
The next president will succeed Dennis J. Shields, who concluded his tenure on Dec.31, 2025. Orlando F. McMeans has served as interim president since Jan. 1.
For more information on the search, go to www.sus.edu/presidentsearch2026.
 
About the Southern University System
The Southern University System is the nation's only historically Black university system, encompassing five campuses and units across Louisiana: Southern University and A&M College, Southern University Law Center, and Southern University Agricultural Research and Extension Center in Baton Rouge; Southern University at New Orleans; and Southern University at Shreveport. The System is committed to providing accessible, high-quality educational opportunities, advancing research and innovation, and serving communities throughout Louisiana and beyond.

item.title: SUBR | Program Coordinator
item.description:
SUBR | Program Coordinator | Position Type: Full-Time Unclassified | Salary: $40,000

Application Deadline: October 23, 2026

 

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Enrollment Management Program Coordinator supports the Division of Enrollment Management at Southern University and A&M College by coordinating recruitment, admissions, financial aid, and student retention initiatives. This position collaborates with internal and external stakeholders to implement programs and strategies that enhance student enrollment, promote student success, and support the University’s mission and enrollment goals.

  •  Receive, sort, and distribute incoming mail and correspondence while maintaining an organized and professional front office environment.
  • Coordinate daily office operations, including managing appointment schedules, maintaining office supplies, and ensuring administrative functions are completed efficiently.
  •  Implement and maintain administrative policies and procedures while providing guidance and training on office management practices.
  • Organize, file, and maintain physical and electronic records, ensuring accuracy, confidentiality, and accessibility.
  • Coordinate travel arrangements for staff, including preparing, processing, and submitting travel documentation in accordance with University policies and procedures.
  • Assist with the coordination and implementation of special projects, programs, and initiatives, including preparing detailed reports and maintaining program documentation.
  • Manage administrative logistics for departmental programs, meetings, events, and forums, including scheduling, communication, preparation of materials, and coordination of resources.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to support the overall operations and objectives of the Division of Enrollment Management.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
  • Three (3) or more years of professional experience in administrative support, office management, program coordination, or a related field.
     

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university.
  • Five (5) or more years of professional experience in administrative support, office management, program coordination, or a related field.
  • Previous experience working in a higher education setting, preferably in enrollment management, admissions, financial aid, or student services.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook) and experience using student information systems, such as Banner.
  • Strong organizational, interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
  • Experience maintaining confidential records, preparing reports, coordinating travel arrangements, and supporting daily office operations.

item.title: SUBR | Student Records Service Representative
item.description:
SUBR | Student Records Service Representative | Position Type: Full-Time Unclassified | Salary: $35,000 - $42,000

Application Deadline: November 8, 2026

 

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Student Records Service Representative provides administrative and customer service support for the Office of the Registrar, including student records management, registration assistance, enrollment verification, transcript processing, and graduation services. This position is responsible for maintaining accurate and confidential academic records, responding to student and departmental inquiries, and ensuring compliance with university policies, Southern University System regulations, and FERPA requirements. The representative works collaboratively with students, faculty, staff, and university departments to support efficient registrar operations and provide timely, professional service.

 

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Maintain and update official student academic records in Banner, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and compliance with university policies, Southern University System regulations, and FERPA requirements.

  • Process student enrollment transactions, including course additions, drops, withdrawals, reinstatements, and curriculum updates in accordance with academic calendars and institutional policies.

  • Review, process, and verify official transcript requests, enrollment certifications, degree verifications, and other academic records requests.

  • Review, process, and verify official transcript requests, enrollment certifications, degree verifications, and other academic records requests.

  • Provide timely and professional customer service to students, faculty, staff, and external agencies regarding academic records, registration, grading, and graduation requirements.

  •  Assist with graduation processing, including reviewing applications, conducting degree audits, and coordinating with academic departments to verify degree requirements.
  •  Support grade processing activities, including posting grades, processing grade changes, resolving discrepancies, and ensuring compliance with established deadlines.
  •  Ensure compliance with university policies, Southern University System requirements, and applicable state and federal regulations related to student records and enrollment reporting.
  •  Assist with maintaining student information systems through data validation, record updates, and coordination with Information Technology and institutional reporting departments.
  •  Respond to records-related inquiries from Financial Aid, Bursar, Academic Affairs, Admissions, Athletics, Veterans Affairs, and other university departments.
  •  Perform other duties as assigned to support the daily operations of the Office of the Registrar, peak processing periods, and special projects.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Two (2) to three (3) years of relevant administrative or customer service experience.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Associate degree from an accredited college or university.

  • Experience working with student records, registration processes, or registrar-related services.

item.title: SUBR | Director of Safety and Risk Management
item.description:
SUBR | Director of Safety and Risk Management | Position Type: Full-Time Unclassified | Salary: $60,000 - $75,000

Application Deadline: November 7, 2026

 

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Director of Safety and Risk Management is responsible for coordinating and directing Southern University and A&M College’s comprehensive safety and risk management program while ensuring compliance with applicable federal, state, and local occupational safety and health regulations.

The Director oversees initiatives designed to identify, assess, and mitigate risks that could impact the University’s safety, security, reputation, operations, or financial well-being. The position also supports compliance with State of Louisiana Office of Risk Management requirements, including maintaining required safety meeting records and coordinating the annual self-audit process.

The incumbent develops, coordinates, and implements policies, procedures, programs, and training to promote effective safety and risk management practices across the University. Key areas of responsibility include accident prevention, safety training, emergency preparedness, loss prevention, regulatory compliance, and risk management.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Develop, implement, and maintain workplace safety policies, procedures, and comprehensive risk management programs.
  • Conduct workplace safety inspections to identify potential hazards and recommend appropriate corrective actions.
  • Coordinate emergency preparedness, evacuation, fire safety, and disaster response plans and procedures.
  • Investigate accidents, injuries, property damage, and other safety-related incidents; prepare reports and recommend corrective and preventive measures.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable OSHA, state, federal, and institutional safety regulations, policies, and requirements.
  • Manage workers’ compensation claims and coordinate with Human Resources, insurance providers, supervisors, and affected employees.
  • Develop and conduct safety training for employees on emergency procedures, workplace hazards, accident prevention, and other safety-related topics.
  • Assess institutional risks and recommend strategies to reduce liability, financial exposure, and potential losses.
  • Maintain accurate safety records, incident reports, inspection documentation, and required regulatory records.
  • Monitor institutional insurance coverage and assist with claims administration, policy renewals, and risk assessments.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned in support of the University’s safety, risk management, and operational needs.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Safety and Health, Safety Management, Risk Management, Environmental Health and Safety, or a closely related field from an accredited college or university.
  • Two (2) to three (3) years of professional experience in safety, occupational health, risk management, or a related area.
  • Experience in safety and risk management within a higher education environment.
  • Knowledge of applicable federal, state, and local occupational safety and health regulations and compliance requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop, implement, and monitor safety policies, procedures, and risk management programs.

item.title: SUBR | Admissions Counselor
item.description:
SUBR | Admissions Counselor | Position Type: Full-Time Unclassified | Salary: $43,888

Application Deadline: October 16, 2026

 

JOB DESCRIPTION:

Reporting to the Assistant Director of Admissions, the Admissions Counselor for Undergraduate Admissions represents Southern University to prospective students, families, schools, and community organizations. This position supports the University’s enrollment goals by generating prospective student interest, increasing inquiries and applications, and assisting students throughout the admissions process from initial contact through enrollment.

The Admissions Counselor works collaboratively with the Admissions Team to develop and implement recruitment strategies designed to achieve established enrollment goals. The position requires excellent customer service, communication, and interpersonal skills and maintains a high level of professionalism in all interactions with prospective students and other stakeholders, including interviews, phone calls, emails, information sessions, recruitment events, and campus visits.

The Admissions Counselor also assists with recruitment initiatives through events, referrals, digital and print communications, and outreach to schools, community organizations, and other external groups. The successful candidate must demonstrate the ability to work independently while also collaborating effectively with students, faculty, staff, administrators, alumni, and other University stakeholders.

JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Communicate with prospective students, parents, families, and community members through appointments, telephone calls, email, and other communication channels.
  • Assist in the development of enrollment marketing materials and communications, including letters, brochures, email campaigns, social media content, and other recruitment materials.
  • Utilize Slate and Banner CRM systems to track and manage prospective student data, generate reports, and support effective communication and outreach efforts.
  • Present information about Southern University, its academic programs, admissions processes, student resources, and the benefits of a Southern University education at high schools, community colleges, recruitment events, and on-campus programs.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with high schools, community colleges, community organizations, and other external partners to strengthen recruitment pipelines and partnerships.
  • Collaborate with internal departments to develop and implement strategic enrollment initiatives using data and insights from CRM systems and other institutional resources.
  • Advise prospective students and families regarding admissions requirements, transfer credits, financial aid opportunities, academic programs, and other enrollment-related matters.

  • Organize and participate in community workshops, recruitment programs, retreats, on-site admissions events, and other enrollment-related activities.

  • Maintain, monitor, and analyze recruitment data to evaluate the effectiveness of outreach initiatives and recommend opportunities for improvement.

  • Develop and implement targeted recruitment strategies based on student enrollment, application, and retention trends.

  • Support the development of departmental goals and objectives and recommend and implement improvements to recruitment processes and operations.

  • Participate in the development and execution of communication workflows within Slate CRM to enhance engagement and responsiveness to prospective students.

  • Maintain accurate prospective and current student information within institutional databases and ensure the confidentiality and appropriate handling of student records.

  • Travel extensively to represent Southern University at recruitment events and activities, including occasional overnight and weekend travel.

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution.

  • Demonstrated experience in student services, admissions, recruitment, financial aid, academic advising, customer service, or a related area.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook.

  • Strong interpersonal, customer service, organizational, and relationship-building skills.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

  • Ability to effectively plan, organize, and manage multiple priorities with strong attention to detail.

  • Ability to analyze recruitment and enrollment data and apply findings to support recruitment strategies and decision-making.

  • Ability to learn and effectively utilize CRM, student information, and enrollment management systems.

  • Ability to work effectively both independently and collaboratively with students, faculty, staff, administrators, and external stakeholders from diverse backgrounds.

  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and appropriately handle student information and records.

  • Valid driver’s license and ability to travel extensively, including occasional overnight travel.

  • Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends during peak recruitment and enrollment periods and University-sponsored events.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • One (1) to two (2) years of professional experience in admissions, student services, recruitment, financial aid, academic advising, or a related higher education environment.

  • Experience using Slate, Banner, PeopleSoft, or comparable CRM, student information, or enrollment management systems.

  • Experience with student recruitment, prospective student outreach, or enrollment management.

  • Experience working with financial aid processes and systems.

  • Experience developing or supporting recruitment communications, outreach campaigns, or enrollment initiatives.

  • Experience using recruitment or enrollment data to evaluate outreach efforts and support strategic decision-making.

Interested applicants must complete a Southern University employment Application.

  • Current Southern University employees should apply here.

  • A cover letter detailing experience and alignment with the role.
  • A curriculum vitae (CV) or resume highlighting expertise and accomplishments.
  • Three (3) professional references.

item.title: Southern University System Presidential Search Committee announces semifinalists
item.description:
The Southern University System Presidential Search Committee today selected semifinalists to advance in the national search for the next president of the Southern University System.

The Search Committee selected the following individuals to advance to the semifinalist stage:

Brian K. Bridges, Ph.D.
Senior Advisor, Whiteboard Advisors
Former Secretary of Higher Education, State of New Jersey (2020-2025)

John K. Belton, J.D.
District Attorney, Third Judicial District Court — Louisiana

Jaffus Hardrick, Ed.D.
Former President, Florida Memorial University 

Roscoe Jones, J.D.
Former Dean, Drake University Law School 

Larissa Littleton-Steib, Ph.D.
Chancellor, Delgado Community College

Willie E. Smith, Ed.D.
Chancellor, Baton Rouge Community College

“Today represents an important milestone in our search for the next president of the Southern University System,” said Jason Hughes, chair, 2026 Southern University System Presidential Search Committee. “Our committee has approached this responsibility thoughtfully and deliberately, recognizing the significance of selecting the individual who will help lead the nation’s only historically Black university system into its next chapter. We are pleased with the progress of the search and look forward to learning more about each of these candidates as we move into the interview phase.”

The selection of semifinalists follows an extensive national search process that has included stakeholder engagement throughout the Southern University System and outreach to prospective candidates. More than 350 students, faculty, staff, administrators, alumni and community stakeholders participated in engagement sessions earlier this year, providing input on the experience, qualities and leadership characteristics desired in the System’s next president.

The Search Committee extends its appreciation to TM² Executive Search, which has assisted the Southern University System throughout the national search process. The firm has worked with the committee to facilitate stakeholder engagement, develop the presidential prospectus, conduct candidate outreach and research, and guide the committee through the evaluation and selection process.

“The committee is grateful to TM² Executive Search for its guidance and expertise throughout this process,” Hughes said. “Their work, along with the valuable input we received from stakeholders across the Southern University System, has helped us conduct a comprehensive search focused on identifying highly qualified leaders who understand both the opportunities and responsibilities associated with leading this historic System.”

Next Steps

The semifinalists will be invited to participate in in-person interviews with the Presidential Search Committee in the coming weeks. Following those interviews, the committee will determine which candidates will advance to the finalist stage of the search process.

Additional information regarding the interview process and subsequent steps in the presidential search will be announced as details are finalized.

The Southern University System launched the national search following the departure of its previous president. The Presidential Search Committee includes representatives from across the Southern University System and the broader community and is charged with recommending finalists for consideration by the Southern University Board of Supervisors.

About the Southern University System

The Southern University System is the nation’s only historically Black university system and includes Southern University and A&M College, Southern University at New Orleans, Southern University at Shreveport, Southern University Law Center and the Southern University Agricultural Research and Extension Center. Through teaching, research and service, the System is committed to providing educational access and opportunity while developing leaders and strengthening communities throughout Louisiana and beyond.

item.title: Southern University System celebrates scholarship support and student success at 2nd annual Southern Celebrates Scholarship Event
item.description:
The Southern University System hosted its second annual Southern Celebrates Scholarship Event Wednesday at the Southern University Welcome Center, bringing together more than 300 benefactors, corporate partners and student scholars from across the Southern University System to celebrate the impact of scholarships, mentorship and partnerships on student success.

The morning brunch highlighted the contributions of supporters whose generosity provides direct support to students at Southern University campuses in Baton Rouge, New Orleans and Shreveport. The event also gave benefactors and corporate partners an opportunity to engage with student scholars and Southern University administrative and academic leaders.

This year’s event also marked Southern University’s 146th year of service to Louisiana and the nation. Southern University is the nation’s only Historically Black College and University system.

“Today is about the gratitude we have for our students who excel and raise the bar,” said Dr. Orlando McMeans, interim president of the Southern University System and chancellor of the Southern University Ag Center. “It is equally about gratitude for those who contribute to that excellence — those who give, mentor, provide a network, an ear, or a prayer. We thank you.”

The program featured a moderated panel discussion, “The Power of Partnership: Nutrien & Southern University,” facilitated by Alfred E. Harrell III, president and CEO of the Southern University System Foundation. Panelists included Ebonie Raby, senior adviser for community relations and investment at Nutrien; Dr. Robert Easley, director of advancement for the College of Agriculture, Human and Environmental Sciences at Southern University and A&M College; and Bryan Glass, a Southern University student scholar.

The discussion highlighted the Nutrien Scholarship Fund at Southern University and explored how sustained corporate-university partnerships can create educational opportunities for students from communities across Louisiana.

“Southern’s success is a shared success,” said Harrell. “Every gift, every mentorship, every partnership represented in this room is already at work in the life of a Southern University student. This event is our opportunity to say thank you, and to show our partners exactly what their investment makes possible.”

The second annual Southern Celebrates Scholarship Event was made possible through the support of Dow, Mele Printing, Aramark, Renasant Bank, the Southern University System Foundation and the Southern University System.

For more information about the Southern University System Foundation and its work supporting donor relations, major gift fundraising, legacy giving and corporate partnerships across the Southern University System, contact Biyaka Williams at biyaka@sutrueblue.org.

item.title: College of Sciences and Engineering to host inaugural STEM game day experience Saturday
item.description:
Southern University’s College of Sciences and Engineering will host its inaugural STEM Game Day, sponsored by Google, on Saturday, Sept. 19, from noon to 4 p.m. at the Southern University Welcome Center. The event will bring science, technology, engineering and mathematics to life through hands-on learning, innovation, gaming and career exploration. All STEM Game Day activities will take place at the Welcome Center, with the exception of the e-sports experience, which will be located on the east side of A.W. Mumford Stadium.

The event reflects Southern University’s commitment to expanding access to STEM education, developing the next generation of STEM professionals and strengthening connections among education, industry and the community.

“STEM Game Day is about creating an environment where students can see, touch and experience STEM while imagining themselves as the scientists, engineers, technologists and innovators of tomorrow,” said Lealon Martin, Ph.D., dean of the College of Sciences and Engineering. “By bringing these experiences into the energy and excitement of Southern University Game Day, we have an opportunity to reach students and families in a unique way while strengthening the connection between our university and the communities we serve.”

Designed to combine the excitement and tradition of Southern University game day with opportunities to explore the possibilities of STEM, the event welcomes K-12 students, families, educators, college students, alumni and community members. Participants will have opportunities to engage with Southern University faculty and students, community organizations and industry professionals through interactive activities and demonstrations.

In addition to Google’s sponsorship, participating community and industry partners include STEM NOLA/STEM Global Action Network, SU EDGE, INDUSTRY MAKES and NOLAvate Black, along with additional Southern University and community partners. Together, the organizations will provide opportunities for students to learn directly from professionals, educators, entrepreneurs and innovators.

A central goal of STEM Game Day is to help young people recognize that STEM extends beyond classrooms and laboratories and plays a role in fields such as gaming, sports, transportation, health care, manufacturing, energy, computing, artificial intelligence and entrepreneurship. By introducing K-12 students to STEM in a fun and welcoming environment, the College of Sciences and Engineering seeks to encourage students to explore STEM coursework, college majors and career opportunities.

College students will also have opportunities to engage with industry and community partners, learn about career pathways and connect their academic experiences to real-world applications. Alumni and community members are invited to participate and support the next generation of STEM leaders.

For more information, including registration, click here. Interested participants must create an account to register.

From tax credits to civil procedure, ethics and professionalism, Southern University Law Center (SULC) Tax Law students recently explored the complexities of legal practice during a visit with the Louisiana Board of Tax Appeals.

Each student attended hearings featuring legal issues such as historic and motion picture tax credits. The proceedings provided students with a firsthand look into how tax matters are presented and resolved, while also addressing issues of civil procedure, professionalism, and ethics that arose during the hearings.

Students also observed two other proceedings involving self- represented litigants, including an exception of prescription and a follow up status conference on a motion to compel. The cases presented an opportunity for the students to see legal concepts in motion and gain firsthand insight into how key issues can arise in practice.

“Our Tax Law Clinic along with Clinical Tax Professor Christian Fasullo, observed the Louisiana Board of Tax Appeals on September 3. This exciting opportunity exposed our student attorneys to state tax litigation matters, the legal practice, and the tax judicial system in action," said Virginia Listach, SULC Professor and Director of Clinical Legal Education. "As an additional bonus, our clinical students will provide a valuable resource to the tax court by assisting self-represented litigants (SRLs) with tax forms and aid the tax court in the development of a self-help SRL legal resource page.”

After the hearings concluded, the students participated in meaningful discussions that connected the day’s proceedings to their legal education. The Louisiana Board of Tax Appeals chairman provided an overview of the history of the Board, giving insight into its purpose and responsibilities.

During the visit, they also discussed the self-represented litigants and received an overview of taxation in Louisiana and the application of tax credits. 

Students within SULC’s Tax Law Clinic will continue their hands-on learning with the Louisiana Board of Tax Appeals during hearings in October and November.

Experiential learning opportunities such as this allow SULC students to see how legal concepts discussed in the classroom translate into real-world practice. By observing proceedings and engaging in discussions with legal professionals, students can further develop the knowledge and skills needed to become practice-ready attorneys.

item.title: Updated Louisiana law heightens penalties for marijuana use on college campuses
item.description:
FROM THE OFFICE OF LOUISIANA GOVERNOR JEFF LANDRY

MARIJUANA ON CAMPUS IS A CRIME

LOUISIANA LAW CHANGED ON AUGUST 1, 2026

 

WHERE THE LAW APPLIES

On campus property. Within 2,000 feet of campus property.

The statute defines "school" to include any public or private college or university in Louisiana and any vocational- technical school. It reaches any person, so it applies to employees and visitors as well as students.

La. R.S. 40:981.3(A), (C)(1)

 

WHAT CHANGED ON AUGUST 1, 2026

Act 305 of the 2026 Regular Session set a new penalty for marijuana possession in a school zone: imprisonment, with or without hard labor, for up to one year, plus a fine of up to $1,000. Before August 1, possessing 14 grams or less carried a fine of up to $100.

La. R.S. 40:981.3(E); La. R.S. 40:966(C)(2)(a)(i)

 

THE ZONE REACHES WELL PAST CAMPUS

Two thousand feet is more than a third of a mile measured out from the property line. On most Louisiana campuses that ring takes in apartments, dorms, fraternity and sorority houses, parking and tailgating lots.

La. R.S. 40:981.3(A)(1)

 

SMOKING AND VAPING ARE COVERED

Act 305 added a new paragraph reaching anyone who violates the drug laws "while smoking, vaping, or otherwise abusing" a controlled dangerous substance in these locations. A THC vape pen counts. Students or guests who possess a prescription order to possess marijuana are not exempt from legal recourse if smoking on school property. La. R.S. 40:981.3(A)(4)

 

THIS IS FELONY-LEVEL EXPOSURE

Louisiana defines a felony as any crime for which the offender may be sentenced to imprisonment at hard labor. The new penalty allows a sentence at hard labor. A conviction goes on an adult criminal record.

La. R.S. 14:2(4)

 

"I DIDN'T KNOW I WAS NEAR A SCHOOL" IS NOT A DEFENSE

The statute states that lack of knowledge that the act occurred on or within 2,000 feet of school property is not a defense.

La. R.S. 40:981.3(B)

 

PENALTIES

UP TO ONE YEAR IN PRISON 

With or without hard labor.

UP TO A $1,000 FINE 

In addition to imprisonment.

item.title: Southern University Chancellor Pierre introduces elevated tailgate experience to benefit student scholarship fund
item.description:
Southern University and A&M College Chancellor John K. Pierre is introducing Lacumba’s Lair, an elevated football tailgate experience designed to bring Southern alumni, supporters, friends and Jaguar fans together while supporting the university’s students.

The inaugural Lacumba’s Lair experience will take place Saturday, Sept. 5, from 2 p.m. through game time at the Southern University Welcome Center. The event will honor legendary Southern football coach Pete Richardson, celebrating his extraordinary legacy and impact on Jaguar football. This gathering is also during the first home football game of the season, aptly named the Pete Richardson Classic.

“We wanted to create something that captures the energy, pride and tradition that make Southern game days special,” Pierre said. “Lacumba’s Lair is about bringing our Jaguar family together, celebrating our history and creating new traditions while investing in the future of our students.”

Lacumba’s Lair will feature Louisiana-inspired cuisine, beverages, a live DJ and musical entertainment, interactive activations, game-viewing screens, photo opportunities, and indoor and outdoor hospitality spaces. Guests may choose between the Lair Experience and a limited-availability Premium Lair Experience, which includes preferred parking, reserved seating, premium hospitality and an exclusive game-day experience.

Advance ticket purchase is required, and guests are asked to wear white, the color of the first home football game of the season. Football game tickets or access to the A.W. Mumford Stadium are not included with the Lacumba’s Lair experience.

Proceeds from Lacumba’s Lair will support the Chancellor’s Access and Opportunity Fund.

For tickets and more information, go to foundation.sus.edu/lacumbas-lair.

item.title: SULC Faculty Share Expertise at 2026 SEALS Annual Conference
item.description:
Southern University Law Center Professors Donna Schwab, Judd Sneirson, and Carlo Pedrioli represented SULC at the 2026 Southeastern Association of Law Schools (SEALS) Annual Conference in Amelia Island, Florida.

Professor Schwab participated in the discussion group “Teaching and Researching in Civil and Comparative Law,” while Professor Sneirson participated in the discussion “Corporate Purpose and Misconduct” and a New Scholars Panel. Professor Pedrioli coordinated and co-chaired the discussion “Voting Rights and Redistricting: The U.S. Supreme Court Decides Louisiana v. Callais.” 

They also explored emerging topics in the legal field, including AI and the NextGen Bar Exam.

We’re proud to see our faculty contributing to important conversations shaping the future of legal education and the legal profession!
